2. The relevant facts necessary for the disposal of this civil appeal are that the predecessor of respondents No.1 (a)-1(c) namely, Dr. Ashequr Rahman Khan as petitioner filed Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1998 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sereenagor, Munshigonj under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for pre-emption of .26 acre of land as appended to the petition. The petitioner's case, in a nutshell, is that he is a co-sharer in the case holding by way of settlement from Kazi Shamsul Huda and others. No statutory notice was served upon the pre-emptor before the alleged transfer. He came to know about the alleged transfers dated 23.09.1981 and the decree as to the declaration of title to the case land in favor of the pre-emptee in Title Suit No. 7 of 1990 only on 12.01.1998. Subsequently, by way of an amendment brought on 05.04.1999, it was stated that the pre-emptor came to know about the alleged Kabalas No. 5315, 5317 & 5319 dated 23.09.1981 and the decree from on Bazlar Rahman. Neither the vendor nor the pre-emptee possesses the case land while the pre-emptor and other co-sharers are in possession thereof. 3. The appellants as pre-emptee contested the case by filing written objection and additional written objection denying all the material allegations made in the pre-emption application and contended, inter alia, that the pre-emption application was barred by limitation. The pre-emptor was not a co-sharer in the case holding, One Shova Rani being the rightful owner of the case land transferred the same in favour of the pre-emptee by three registered sale deeds and delivered possession thereof to her. As the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Sreenagor theatened to lease out the case land treating the same as Khas land, the pre-emptee instituted Title Suit No. 7 of 1990 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sreenagar for declaration of title and permanent injunction in respect of the case land and upon trial the said suit was decreed and as such the pre-emption case is liable to be rejected. 

 9. In opposition, Mr. Muhammad Ruhul Amin Bhuiyan, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents No. 1(a)-1(c) vehemently opposes the submissions put forth on behalf of the appellant. The learned Counsel contends that the High Court Division has committed illegality in disposing of the Rule without discussing on the question of limitation and the statement given by the pre-emptor regarding the cases of action, which was only ground for dismissal of appeal by the appellate Court. The learned Counsel contends next that the trial Court most illegally disallowed the pre-emption case and the appellate Court unlawfully affirmed the judgment of the trial Court, and thereafter, the High Court Division committed illegality by disposing of the revisional application filed by the pre-emptor inasmuch as the High Court Division did not dispose of the Rule in the light of the provision of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned counsel lastly craves for dismissal of the instant appeal. 

 11. At the outset, let us examine whether the Pre-emption Case No. 17 of 1998 is barred by limitation. The pre-emptor claims that he came to know about the alleged transfer on 12.01.1998 from the localities in his village home. One Dr. Ataur Rahman the younger brother of the pre-emptor deposed before the court on behalf of the pre-emptor as P.W.1 But P.W.1 did not state in his examination-in-chief about the person from whom the pre-emptor learnt about the alleged transfer. Although P.W.1 stated in his cross-examination that the pre-emptor came to know about the alleged sale from his caretaker named Bazlur Rahman. Thereafter the pre-emptor by an amendment petition on 05.04.1999 claimed that he came to know about the transfer in question from his caretaker named Bazlur Rahman. But P.W. 1 did not utter a single word as to why the pre-emptor could not know about the alleged sale deeds for such a long time. Moreover, it has not been stated in the pre-emption petition as to when said Bazlur Rhaman came to know first about the alleged sale deed. Therefore, it is evident that the pre-emptor filed the pre-emption petition long after 17 years from the date of execution of the alleged sale deeds. 

 12. Again, P.W.1 stated in his cross-examination that he used to visit his village house regularly at 2/3 months interval and he came to know about the alleged sale deeds during the pendency of Civil Suit No. 07 of 1990 filed by the pre-emptee regarding the suit land.
